To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

InsP3 receptors redistribute into large aggregates in the ER and nuclear envelope of antigen-stimulated RBL cells and that this redistribution is independent of vesiculation of the ER and is calcium-dependent.

InsP3 receptors redistribute to large clusters in a calcium-dependent manner in three different cell types, and that this redistribution is a common cellular response to stimulation of phospholipases C linked to either G protein or receptor tyrosine kinases.
stimulation of phospholipases C leads to the calcium-dependent aggregation of inositol-1,4, 5-trisphosphatereceptors in a variety of cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of calcium in the regulation of intracellular calcium release.
understanding the mechanisms by which cells regulate their intracellular calcium levels.
the role of calcium in the clustering of InsP3 receptor in rat basophilic leukemia cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
InsP3 receptor redistribution in RBL-2h3 cells is a calcium dependent event, which is not dependent on the presence or absence of agonist.
calcium-dependent clustering of inositrol-1,4, 5-trisphosphatereceptors occurs in response to a wide variety of stimuli in a variety of cells.

calcium-dependent clustering of inositide 1,4.5-trisphosphatereceptors is a common feature of cells with a variety of receptor types and that this clustering is independent of receptor down-regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
InsP3 receptors aggregate into large clusters within minutes of stimulation of cells with a Ca2+-mibolizing ligand and that this process is dependent on the presence and/or concentration of Ca2+.
InsP3 receptors are calcium sensors that regulate the amount of calcium released from stores and the affinity of the InsP3 receptor for InsP3.
the type II InsP 3 receptors are the major receptors in RBL cells and they are clustered in response to FcepsilonR1 activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the type II InsP 3 receptor is the primary receptor expressed in rat basophilic leukemia-2H3 (RBL- 2H3) and AR4-2 J cells and is a target of the calcium-dependent aggregation.
the InsP3 receptor is a dynamic protein that can be recruited to sites of Ca2+ release.
calcium can induce the clustering of inosital triphosphate receptors, which is a process that may contribute to the regulation of calcium signaling in cells.
